items.q: Roy Eldridge, Lester Young, Ray Brown, Joe Benjamin and Norman Grantz the organiser of the J.A.T.P. came to the cocktail.

ctx.x: I assisted in one of the post picturesque weddings I had ever seen. This happened in a part of Paris known as the Commune libre de la Butte Montmarte which is the surrounding of the famous Sacred Heart Church (Sacré Coeur). The marriage was that of a well known Gipsy Violinist Roman Jacowlew to a Miss Pilar Gonzales, a spanish actress. After the wedding ceremony, I lead a parade of montmartrois and Montmartroises (as the people from the Butte Montmarte are called) are dressed in picturesque clothes from the last…

A few days later, the Jazz at Philharmonic was giving a concert at Salle Pleyel. I knew weeks before when they would be in town,so Lilly arranged for me to give a cocktail party for them at the reception offices of Ricard, the makers of the well known appetizer. Roy Eldridge, Lester Young, Ray Brown, Joe Benjamin and Norman Grantz the organiser of the J.A.T.P. came to the cocktail. But there is a story about this cocktail that was very embarrassing for me.
The cocktail was supposed to start at 6 p.m. and finished at 8, and as I was the host, I was supposed to be there before the guests

items.q: This must have been at the beginning of Norman Grant's presentation of jazz at the Philharmonic which became famous in later years.

ctx.x: Al Hall had introduced me to Nat Cole a few years before, and also Oscar Moore, who was Nat's guitarist. They were playing at Kelly's Stable then, and had not become very well known. I had never heard of or met Max Roach, and Kay Starr was a west coast singer that I had not heard about also. We recorded four numbers, and one included "Stormy Weather", which Kay sang, and "If I Could Be With You One Hour Tonight". I had recorded with Benny before, and Coleman Hawkins in 1943, but this recording intrigued me more…

A few nights later Kirby was engaged to do a concert along with some other musicians at the Philharmonic Opera House in Los Angeles. This must have been at the beginning of Norman Grant's presentation of jazz at the Philharmonic which became famous in later years.

Coleman Hawkins asked me if I would work a couple of weeks with him at Shepp's PlayHouse. Howard McGee was supposed to have come to Los Angeles with him, but did not show up when Hawk started. I don't remember any of the other musicians that were in the group, but it was another great moment in my life to be playing a Club date with the one and only Hawkins, and I enjoyed every moment of it.
